statements.t: We expect staking yields to evolve with validator participation rates, protocol parameters and market conditions.

Where we deploy ETH to staking or analogous activities, we intend to size exposures conservatively, prioritize best-in-class custody and validator operations (including multi-client diversity and performance monitoring), and maintain appropriate unencumbered liquidity to meet corporate needs.
As an ETH-focused company, we expect a mix shift in operating expenses toward cybersecurity, custody, treasury operations, compliance and technology enablement for advisory and analytics.
We intend to maintain a flexible cost structure aligned with services activity and treasury scale.

We intend to maintain sufficient liquidity to support operations, regulatory compliance, and security investments, while seeking opportunities to increase ETH holdings when market conditions are attractive.
After completion of this contract, the Company does not expect to generate any further revenue from this source.

Because our digital assets are measured at fair value, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings, changes in ETH prices are expected to continue to cause significant volatility in our reported results, stockholders’ equity and financial condition.

A sustained decline in ETH prices could reduce the value of our asset base and staking revenue, limit our ability to raise capital on acceptable terms and require us to sell ETH or other assets to satisfy operating or liquidity requirements.
Our future revenue and cash generation are therefore expected to depend substantially on the amount of ETH staked, ETH prices, validator performance and prevailing staking yields.

In addition, validator downtime, slashing, cybersecurity incidents, software defects, infrastructure failures or protocol changes could reduce rewards, result in the loss of staked ETH or adversely affect our ability to provide staking services.
We expect to continue incurring infrastructure, personnel, cybersecurity, custody, compliance and monitoring costs as we expand these activities.

If MAVAN does not achieve the operating performance, customer growth or anticipated benefits considered in the acquisition analysis, or if market conditions deteriorate, we may be required to record impairment charges or additional measurement-period adjustments.

We expect this arrangement to reduce and simplify the fee structure applicable to the covered staking activities, although the actual fees will vary with staking rewards and the amount of eligible ETH staked.
A concurrent decline in ETH prices and staking yields could reduce our available cash generation and dividend coverage.
Accordingly, a failure to pay dividends when expected could increase our obligations, adversely affect the market price of the preferred stock and limit our financial flexibility.
We expect the costs of custody, cybersecurity, insurance, monitoring and compliance to remain significant and to increase as the scale and complexity of our operations grow.

We expect to file a transition report on Form 10-KT for the four-month period from September 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 and a quarterly report on Form 10-QT for the three months ended November 30, 2026.
We expect the following material cash requirements over the next 12 months under our capital-light model:
• fees that will be incurred from industry-experienced third parties to manage the Company’s multi-billion dollar ETH portfolio.

The Company expects these fees to be significantly offset by projected staking fees earned from the same ETH portfolio, although there can be no assurances that the Company will be successful in doing so;

• cash dividend obligations related to the Company's outstanding 9.50% Series A Preferred Stock, which are expected to approximate $33.3 million over the next 12 months based on the current dividend rate and shares outstanding.

We believe, based on our current operating plan, expected cash on hand, anticipated operating cash flows and access to capital under our shelf/ATM, that we will have sufficient liquidity to fund operations for at least the next 12 months.
We do not expect to enter into new long-term power purchase or build-to-suit arrangements absent clear, low-risk returns.
We will update our critical accounting estimates as our operations evolve and additional trends and data become reasonably available.
